messages:
mira: heads-up — I ran a replay-harness vs synthetic-load comparison for llama2-13b-q4 using the same prompt set and decoding params. quick summary: synthetic looks ~8% faster avg, but replay p99 is ~12% worse. profiler points at KV cache churn + a kernel fallback on longer prefixes.

alex: can you paste the harness commands and the key profiler snippets? also which stop sequences were used?

mira: command I used:
```
./perf-harness --mode=replay --model=llama2-13b-q4 --prompts=tests/replay_prompts.json \
  --decode="temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=[\\"\\n\\",\\"\\n\\n\\"]" --concurrency=64 --duration=300
```
stop sequences are literally ["\\n","\\n\\n"] — same file used for synthetic. tokenizer config = `sentencepiece-v1` (but see below).

perf-bot: perf report uploaded: /artifacts/perf/1750001234/replay-vs-synth/index.html

jamal: profiler flame summary (sampled stacks):
```
flash_attn_fwd           41%
matmul_256x128           18%
kv_cache_lookup          15%  <- much higher in replay
fallback_gemm_generic    12%  <- kernel selector chose generic path for some shapes
other                    14%
```
p99 latency: synthetic=210ms, replay=235ms. avg: synthetic=45ms, replay=49ms.

sara: interesting. kv_cache_lookup being 15% suggests we're not hitting prefix reuse as effectively under replay. are prompts longer on average? did you align tokenizers between the harness and the model? mismatched tokenizer can add tokens and change the chunking/k-v hit rate.

mira: prompts are same file — but double-checked: the replay harness was using the local `sp-tokenizer` binary (v1.2.0) while the model container has a slightly different sentencepiece table (v1.1.9). so yes, tokenizer mismatch likely. that would explain extra tokens and more cache pressure.

ken: also note the kernel selector fallback: the profiler shows `fallback_gemm_generic` at 12%. logs show this pattern:
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] kernel_selector: chose matmul_sm80_fast for (M=512, N=128)
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] kernel_selector: fallback to generic_gemm for (M=1024, N=64) due to unsupported tile config
```
that can happen when input lengths produce matrix shapes we haven't optimized for. replay sequences had longer prefixes in many samples.

alex: ok — so two main levers: 1) fix tokenizer alignment in the harness, 2) expand kernel selector rules / add tuned kernels for the shapes we saw. which should we do first?

mira: tokenizer alignment is quick — I'll pin the harness to the exact sentencepiece model used in the container and re-run. after that we should re-evaluate; if p99 gap persists we'll iterate on kernel selector.

sara: small note on decoding params — ensure `eos` handling is identical. some harnesses strip trailing whitespace before stop-match which can change tokenization of stops. we should normalize: `normalize_whitespace=true` and use the same stop matching codepath as the runtime (use `runtime.stop_match`).

jamal: attaching a small diff I used to make the harness match runtime behavior:
```
- tokens = sp.encode(prompt)
+ prompt_norm = runtime_normalize(prompt)
+ tokens = sp.encode(prompt_norm)
```
runtime_normalize does: unicode_nfc, collapse_spaces, ensure trailing newline preserved.

perf-bot: scheduled rerun job (job id: 1750000012) pinned tokenizer=v1.1.9, normalize=true, same decode params.

mira: re-run started. expected ~45m. I'll paste results when done.

ken: long term we should add a harness check that fails if tokenizer fingerprint != model.tokenizer_fingerprint. low-cost guard.

alex: agreed. also add a kernel selector telemetry alert if fallback_gemm_generic > 5% over a 10m window — we can auto-schedule an offline bench to create optimized kernels.

mira: plan recorded: 1) fix tokenizer pin + normalization (in progress) 2) rerun replay vs synthetic 3) if regression remains, capture representative shapes and add to kernel build bench 4) add harness preflight checks and selector alerts. will update thread with numbers.

sara: :thumbsup: thanks mira — nice detective work.

mira: done for now — dropping the perf link here when the new run finishes.
